guides.title: Docker daemon socket permission denied
patterns: permission denied while trying to connect to the docker daemon socket
got permission denied while trying to connect
guides.summary: The CLI cannot access /var/run/docker.sock because your user is not in the docker group or the socket permissions changed.
symptoms: Every docker command fails, including docker ps
docker version prints the Client section but not the Server section
causes: User is not a member of the docker group
Group membership was added but the session has not been refreshed
A rootless or remote context requires different access

steps.title: Check membership
steps.detail: Run `id` and look for the docker group. If it is missing, add the user and start a new login session.

steps.title: Add the group
steps.detail: On Linux, add the user to the docker group. This is root-equivalent access; treat it accordingly.

steps.title: Refresh the session
steps.detail: Log out and back in, or start a new shell with the updated group.

steps.title: Verify
steps.detail: Confirm the daemon is reachable.

guides.title: Port is already allocated
guides.summary: The host port you asked Docker to publish is already bound by another process or container.
symptoms: Container fails to start with a port binding error
Works on a different host port
causes: Another container is publishing the same host port
A host process (nginx, node, a database) owns the port
A previous container was stopped but not removed, keeping the name/port reservation in some cases

steps.title: Identify the listener
steps.detail: Find the process or container holding the port.

steps.title: Check Docker
steps.detail: List published ports and find the owner.

steps.title: Choose a free port
steps.detail: Use a different host port, ideally on loopback.

steps.title: Remove the stale container if appropriate
steps.detail: Only if it is genuinely no longer needed.

guides.title: Image not found or pull access denied
guides.summary: The registry cannot find the repository/tag, or the request is not authenticated for a private image.
symptoms: docker pull fails before any container starts
Compose up fails with "pull access denied"
causes: Tag typo or a tag that was never pushed
Image is private and you are not logged in
Registry host is missing from the reference (defaults to Docker Hub)
Architecture manifest does not exist for --platform

steps.title: Read the full reference
steps.detail: Confirm registry host, repository and tag. A missing host means Docker Hub.

steps.title: Authenticate
steps.detail: Log in to the registry with a scoped token.

steps.title: Check tags
steps.detail: List available tags through the registry API or UI.

steps.title: Pin a known tag
steps.detail: Use a tag that exists and matches your architecture.

guides.title: Container exits with code 127
guides.summary: The command in ENTRYPOINT/CMD does not exist in the image or cannot be resolved through PATH.
symptoms: Container exits immediately
docker logs is empty or shows "executable file not found"
causes: Wrong binary name or path
Shell used in exec form with arguments
Base image changed and removed the tool
Entrypoint script has CRLF line endings or no executable bit

steps.title: Read state
steps.detail: Check exit code, error and command.

steps.title: Inspect the image
steps.detail: Override the entrypoint with a shell and check the filesystem.

steps.title: Verify PATH
steps.detail: Find the binary and confirm it is executable.

steps.title: Fix the Dockerfile
steps.detail: Use exec form with the absolute path, or install the missing runtime.

guides.title: Container killed with exit code 137
guides.summary: The process received SIGKILL, commonly because it exceeded the container memory limit.
symptoms: Container restarts repeatedly
docker inspect shows OOMKilled=true
No application stack trace
causes: --memory limit too low
JVM/Node heap not aware of the cgroup limit
Memory leak
Host under memory pressure

steps.title: Confirm OOM
steps.detail: Check OOMKilled and exit code.

steps.title: Measure usage
steps.detail: Compare usage to the limit over time.

steps.title: Tune the runtime
steps.detail: Set heap limits or raise the container limit deliberately.

steps.title: Fix the leak
steps.detail: If usage grows without bound, profile the application rather than increasing the limit forever.

guides.title: No space left on device
guides.summary: The Docker data root, a volume, or the host filesystem is full.
symptoms: Containers fail to start or write
Images fail to pull
Builds fail with ENOSPC
causes: Build cache growth
Unrotated container logs
Large unused images
A volume containing database or application data
Host disk genuinely full

steps.title: Measure
steps.detail: See Docker usage by category and find the host mount.

steps.title: Inspect the host
steps.detail: Find the largest directories under the Docker root.

steps.title: Prune with retention
steps.detail: Remove build cache and unused images, not volumes you need.

steps.title: Fix logs
steps.detail: Configure log rotation and recreate affected containers.

steps.title: Back up volumes before pruning
steps.detail: Never run volume prune on a host with unbacked data.

guides.title: Service name does not resolve
guides.summary: Containers cannot resolve a service name, usually because they are not on the same user-defined network.
symptoms: Database connection fails by name
Works with an IP but not a hostname
Works for some services and not others
causes: Containers are on the default bridge instead of a user-defined network
Service is on a different network
Typo in the service name
The dependency is not running yet

steps.title: Check networks
steps.detail: List each container’s networks and addresses.

steps.title: Check membership
steps.detail: Inspect the network and confirm both services are attached.

steps.title: Test from inside
steps.detail: Resolve the name from the client container.
steps.command: docker exec CLIENT getent hosts SERVICE

steps.title: Fix attachment
steps.detail: Connect the container to the shared network, or fix the Compose network configuration.

guides.title: Build fails with network or DNS errors
guides.summary: The build container cannot reach package registries or internal mirrors.
symptoms: npm/pip/apt install fails inside RUN
Build works locally but not in CI
DNS errors only during build
causes: Daemon DNS configuration issues
Proxy not passed to the build
Corporate registry/mirror required
IPv6 or firewall issues
Base image lacks CA certificates

steps.title: Reproduce the layer
steps.detail: Build the target stage and open a shell to test connectivity.
steps.command: docker build --target build -t dbg . && docker run --rm -it dbg sh

steps.title: Pass proxy settings
steps.detail: Use build args or daemon proxy configuration for HTTP(S)_PROXY.

steps.title: Check DNS
steps.detail: Test resolution inside the build stage.

steps.title: Use a mirror
steps.detail: Configure the package manager to use an internal mirror if the public registry is blocked.

guides.title: Compose file is invalid
guides.summary: The resolved Compose model is invalid or a variable is missing.
symptoms: docker compose up fails before creating anything
Interpolation warning or empty value
Schema validation error
causes: YAML indentation error
Unknown or misspelled property
Missing variable referenced with ${...}
Top-level version or legacy syntax

steps.title: Validate
steps.detail: Run config --quiet to get a precise error.

steps.title: Print the resolved model
steps.detail: See exactly what Compose will send to the engine.

steps.title: Fix interpolation
steps.detail: Provide defaults or fail-fast values.

steps.title: Remove obsolete version
steps.detail: Modern Compose ignores the top-level version key; remove it.

guides.title: Service stays unhealthy
guides.summary: The health check command is failing, so dependent services never start.
symptoms: docker ps shows (unhealthy)
Compose dependency waits forever
Application responds but health check fails
causes: Health check uses a tool not present in the image
Wrong endpoint or port
Start period too short
Dependency genuinely unavailable
Health check checks localhost inside the wrong container

steps.title: Read the health log
steps.detail: Inspect the last probe output.

steps.title: Run the probe manually
steps.detail: Execute the health check command inside the container.

steps.title: Check the endpoint
steps.detail: Confirm the app listens on the expected interface and port.

steps.title: Adjust timings
steps.detail: Increase start_period and retries for slow starters.

guides.title: Permission denied writing to a volume
guides.summary: The container user cannot write to the mounted path, or the filesystem is mounted read-only.
symptoms: App starts then crashes on first write
Works as root but not as the app user
Bind mount works on one host only
causes: UID/GID mismatch between container user and host path
Directory does not exist or wrong ownership
read_only root filesystem without a writable mount
SELinux label missing on a bind mount

steps.title: Check identity
steps.detail: Compare the container user to the mount ownership.
steps.command: docker exec NAME id; ls -ln HOST_PATH

steps.title: Check mounts
steps.detail: Confirm read/write flags.

steps.title: Fix ownership
steps.detail: Chown the host path or run with a matching user. Prefer named volumes.

steps.title: SELinux
steps.detail: Add :z or :Z to the bind mount on SELinux hosts.

guides.title: Registry TLS or certificate error
patterns: http: server gave http response to https client
guides.summary: Docker does not trust the registry certificate, or the registry is using HTTP where TLS is required.
symptoms: Login or push fails with certificate errors
Works for Docker Hub but not an internal registry
causes: Self-signed or internal CA not installed in the Docker trust store
Registry served over plain HTTP
Hostname mismatch in the certificate
Proxy intercepting TLS

steps.title: Verify the endpoint
steps.detail: Check the certificate chain and hostname.

steps.title: Install the CA
steps.detail: Place the internal CA in /etc/docker/certs.d/REGISTRY/ca.crt on the client.

steps.title: Prefer TLS
steps.detail: Do not use insecure-registries for anything beyond a local lab.

steps.title: Restart the daemon
steps.detail: Reload or restart after installing certificates.
